intro: These elevated connectors are rarely new in meaning — most of them have an everyday twin you already know (aber, obwohl, weil, trotzdem, deshalb) — but they differ in register, in the exact logical relation they express and, crucially, in the word order they trigger. This quiz drills 16 sentences: indes / indessen as adversative “however” and as temporal “meanwhile”; wiewohl, obschon, obgleich and wenn auch as elevated concessive connectors; zumal (da) for “especially as”; gleichwohl, nichtsdestoweniger and dessen ungeachtet as concessive adverbs with verb-second order; mithin and somit for a logical conclusion; insofern als and the split insoweit …, als for restriction; allein as literary “but” outside the clause; and respektive. Every cue gives the English meaning and the word-order slot you must fill, and every synonym that fits both is accepted.
tips[0].title: Three word-order classes
tips[0].text: Subordinators send the verb to the end: wiewohl, obschon, obgleich, obzwar, zumal, insofern als. Adverbs take position 1 (verb second) or sit in the middle field: indes, indessen, gleichwohl, nichtsdestoweniger, dessen ungeachtet, mithin, somit, folglich. Coordinators stand outside the clause (position 0) and change nothing: aber, doch, allein.
tips[0].trap: gleichwohl is not a subordinator in standard German: “…, gleichwohl sie wertvolle Hinweise liefert” is marked as wrong.
tips[0].check.why: The verb follows directly, so position 1 needs an adverb: gleichwohl. wiewohl, obgleich and zumal are subordinators and would send the verb to the end.
tips[1].title: indes / indessen: two meanings
tips[1].text: Adversative “however” (= jedoch), usually in the middle field: Die Betroffenen warten indes bis heute darauf. Temporal “meanwhile” (= währenddessen, unterdessen), usually in position 1: Indessen bereitete der Gastgeber das Dessert vor. The context decides which reading is meant.
tips[1].check.why: Two actions run side by side with no contrast, and indessen opens the clause in position 1: the temporal reading, ‘meanwhile’.
tips[2].title: zumal: the reason that tips the balance
tips[2].text: zumal (da / weil) adds a further, decisive reason to something already stated: “especially as, all the more since”. It is subordinating, so the verb goes to the end, and the zumal-clause normally follows the main clause.
tips[2].check.why: zumal is subordinating, so the finite verb goes to the end of its clause.
tips[3].title: mithin, insofern als, allein, respektive
tips[3].text: mithin (formal “consequently”) draws a logical conclusion, like somit and folglich. insofern als / insoweit als restrict a claim (“in so far as”); the two halves can also be split: nur insoweit bindend, als … . allein at the head of a clause is an elevated “but” and does not invert. respektive (bzw.) links items that correspond one to one.
tips[3].check.why: The second clause is the logical conclusion of the first, so it takes mithin (‘consequently’), an adverb that sits in the middle field.
table.caption: Elevated connectors: meaning and word order
remember[0]: Subordinators (wiewohl, obschon, zumal, insofern als) → verb at the end.
remember[1]: Adverbs (indes, gleichwohl, dessen ungeachtet, mithin) → verb second or in the middle field.
remember[2]: allein = aber in position 0: no inversion.
remember[3]: indes can mean “however” or “meanwhile” — read the context.
mistakes[0].why: gleichwohl is an adverb in standard German: it triggers verb-second order, not verb-final.
mistakes[1].why: zumal is a subordinator: the finite verb goes to the end.
mistakes[2].why: As a conjunction, allein stands in position 0 like aber; the clause keeps its normal order.
hook: Indes, wiewohl, zumal, mithin: the elevated connectors of serious prose — and the word order each one demands.
